item.title: Enforcement and Practicability
item.lead: A model law is only meaningful when the supervisory chain is practically enforceable.

blocks.text: The dossier implicitly argues for a combination of ex ante transparency and ex post enforcement. Platforms, agencies, and processors should provide clear information, while regulators must have access to relevant data and documentation when abuse is suspected.

Chain liability therefore requires a clear definition of factual control. Otherwise, the regulation risks only affecting the formal contractual party while operational power lies elsewhere. The source identifies precisely this mismatch as a significant problem.

Another point of attention is international cooperation. When the creator, agency, payment processor, and chat farm are located in different countries, competencies and procedures can become fragmented. Effective regulation should therefore align with existing European and international mechanisms for data protection, financial compliance, and platform oversight.

The legal agenda of the dossier is ultimately a design question: how do you make the party that benefits economically also sufficiently visible and responsible? The Lex Humanitas Digitalis is in this interpretation a proposal to structurally increase that visibility.
